creator: Alexander Terp
description:
## Why

The Antigravity round (2026-11-21) built and live-checked agy support on this Mac, and left three
behaviors unobserved. Muster, Ordo, memri and Fencil each rely on a guess about them.

## What to observe

1. **Compaction.** Fill an agy conversation until it compacts. Does the session ID change, do the
   session-start hooks run again (Ordo's practices, memri's index, Fencil's notice), does Muster's
   context reading and `muster pane compact` still work, and what does the transcript record?
2. **A hook that misbehaves.** Install a scratch hook that sleeps past agy's timeout, and one that
   prints malformed JSON. Does agy drop the hook's output, fail the turn, or stall? One unexplained
   170 s hang on `gemini-3.8-flash-medium` was seen on 2026-11-21 and may be this.
3. **agy on Linux.** Install agy on a Linux machine and run Muster's adapter there: screen
   detection, the plugin's hooks, transcript provenance (the test that failed on Linux CI covers
   only the report script).

Record what is found in `~/src/tai-personal/docs/antigravity.md`, which lists these as not probed,
and raise a card in the affected tool for anything that breaks.

## Cost and limits

Items 1 and 2 spend Gemini quota: a few Flash turns for the hooks, and a long conversation for
compaction. Run them when the 5-hour Gemini window has room and no benchmark run needs it.

Item 3 waits on the owner: agy must be signed in with his Google account on a Linux machine, and
only he can do that. Which machine is his call; the work devenv is not an obvious fit for a
personal Google login.
title: Antigravity: probe compaction, misbehaving hooks, and agy on Linux
